# Section 030: Scaling

Makes the reader able to tell what limits a Collector and to scale it without losing or duplicating data. It teaches how to read the Collector self-telemetry, how queues, retries, the memory limiter and resource limits protect the process, when replicas behind a Service are enough, and how to route and shard data when a component needs related items in one place, as tail sampling and scrape receivers do.

**Curriculum item covered:** Scaling

---

## What You Will Master

- Read accepted, refused, sent and failed span metrics and the exporter queue size and capacity on port 8888
- Tell a source bottleneck from a processor bottleneck and a destination bottleneck
- Configure `sending_queue`, `retry_on_failure`, `memory_limiter` and `batch` and explain what each does under load
- Choose resource requests, limits and the Go memory limit, and compare vertical with horizontal scaling
- Explain why a long-lived gRPC connection pins to one pod behind a Service
- Route spans by trace ID with the `load_balancing` exporter so that `tail_sampling` sees whole traces
- Shard a `prometheus` receiver with `hashmod` and a StatefulSet so that no target is scraped twice
- Name the Target Allocator and the sources of duplicates that remain after sharding

## The Learning Path

### 1. Capacity Signals And Protecting The Collector
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Capacity Signals And Protecting The Collector](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-030/module-01/playground` — kind cluster with a `gateway` Collector (memory limiter, batch, queue, self-telemetry on port 8888) that exports to a `backend` Collector in `starfleet`, and a `drifter` curl pod in `outpost`.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS075.git -c sections/section-030/module-01/playground
    ```
*   **Hands-on Lab:** `sections/section-030/module-01/labs/lab-01` — expose the gateway metrics, fix the exporter and queue, and add the protection.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS075.git -c sections/section-030/module-01/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```

### 2. Sharding And Stateful Processing
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Sharding And Stateful Processing](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-030/module-02/playground` — kind cluster with a `gateway` that routes by trace ID, two `sampler` pods with `tail_sampling` and a two-pod `scraper` StatefulSet in `starfleet`, and `drifter` in `outpost`.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS075.git -c sections/section-030/module-02/playground
    ```
*   **Hands-on Lab:** `sections/section-030/module-02/labs/lab-01` — replace a plain exporter with trace ID routing so that traces stay whole on one sampler pod.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS075.git -c sections/section-030/module-02/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Scaling Capstone — `sections/section-030/capstone/labs/lab-01`
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS075.git -c sections/section-030/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** Make an unprotected gateway scalable and correct. The reader exposes the self-telemetry, adds the memory limiter and a larger queue, routes spans by trace ID to two samplers and shards the scraper so that each target has one owner. The grader reads the live configuration, sends traces through the gateway and reads the sampler and scraper logs. The lab is untested.
